column1: # intent-exemplars.tsv — labelled phrasings for the embedding intent classifier.
# Valid intents: procedure | troubleshooting | clause_lookup | out_of_scope
# The original classifier was keyword substring matching. Measured on a held-out
# set of 12 engineer-style paraphrases containing no trigger keywords, it scored
# 5/12 (41%) — and 7 of the 12 collapsed to clause_lookup, the default, because
# no term matched. "walk me through how the UE comes back after losing the cell"
# is plainly a procedure question and hit nothing.
# These exemplars are embedded once at startup with the BGE-M3 model already
# loaded for retrieval (no extra model, no network call). A query is classified
# by cosine similarity to its nearest exemplar, which generalises to paraphrases
# the keyword list will never enumerate.
# - Vary the phrasing deliberately: formal spec language, casual engineer speak,
#   and operational/field phrasing all appear for each intent. Similar exemplars
# - Do NOT paste in the held-out evaluation phrases. Tuning exemplars against the
#   eval set makes the measured accuracy meaningless.
# - After editing, re-run the intent eval AND bench/run_bench.py.
# ── procedure: the answer is a sequence of steps across network functions ─────
